la:verb:divulgo.gloss: to spread among the people, make common, publish, divulge
senses: to spread among the people, make common, publish, divulge
la:verb:divulgo.html:
dīvulgo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to spread among the people, to make common, publish, divulge (rare but class.; cf.: publico, vulgo, pervulgo, pervagor): librum,; ; ; cf. seria,: consilium Domitii, * : chirographa omnium,: versiculos,: omnem mimum, et saep.: rem sermonibus,; cf.: aliquid turpi fama,: opinionem tam gloriosae expeditionis,; cf.: hanc opinionem in Macedoniam,.— With acc. and inf.: non est divulgandum de te jam esse perfectum,; cf. —
Transf., to make common: cujus primum tempus aetatis palam fuisset ad omnium libidines divulgatum, lowered or degraded to, Cic. Post. Red. ap. Sen. 5, 11.—Hence, dīvul-gātus, a, um, P. a., widespread: alicujus divulgata gloria,: divulgata veris ante habere,: Afer divulgato ingenio,: magistratus levissimus et divulgatissimus (sc. praeturae),i. e. most common,.—Comp. and adv. do not occur.

la:noun:divortium.html:
dīvortĭum (†
divertium,), ii, n.
diverto
, a separation.
In gen.: ubi illud quod volo habebo ab illo, facile invenio, quomodo divortium et discordiam inter nos parem, (with a play on II. 1 infra): neutrubi habebo stabile stabulum, siquid divorti fuat,.—
Esp.
A divorce, dissolution of marriage (by consent; opp. repudium, compulsory divorce by either party; cf. ); orig. used only of the wife: uxori sit reddunda dos divortio,; ; ; ; Cael. ap. ; but afterwards in gen.,: et Lentulum cum Metella certe fecisse divortium,; ; ; ; ; ; et saep.—
Concr., a point of separation, place where a road divides, a fork in a road, ; cf. itinerum,: artissimo inter Europam Asiamque divortio Byzantium posuere Graeci,.—So, aquarum, i. e. a summit whence the streams run different ways, a water-shed, ; ; .—
Trop.
Ex communi sapientium jugo sunt doctrinarum facta divortia, etc., divisions, varieties, .—
Veris et hiemis, the time at which winter ends and spring begins, .—
Alta divortia riparum, lofty opposite banks, . —
Tanto rerum divortio, opposition, inconsistency, Ap. de Mundo, p. 66, 9: anima nullum init cum sua unitate divortium,.

la:verb:divido.html:
dī-vĭdo, vīsi, vīsum, 3 (
perf. sync. divisse, ), v. a.
root vidh-, to part, split; Sanscr. vidhyati, to penetrate, whence vidhava; Lat. vidua
.
To force asunder, part, separate, divide (very freq. and class.; cf.: distribuo, dispertio; findo, scindo, dirimo, divello, separo, sejungo, segrego, secerno).
Lit.: Europam Libyamque rapax ubi dividit unda, Enn. ap. ; and : discludere mundum membraque dividere,; cf.: si omne animal secari ac dividi potest, nullum est eorum individuum,: crassum aërem, (with perrumpere); cf. nubila,: muros,to break through,: marmor cuneis,to split,; cf.: hunc medium securi,: mediam frontem ferro,; also simply, insulam, for to divide into two parts, .—Poet.: vagam caelo volucrem,i. e. to cleave, to shoot,: sol ... in partes non aequas dividit orbem,; so Galliam in partes tres,: vicum in duas partes flumine,: civitatem Helvetiam in quatuor pagos,: populum unum in duas partes,; cf. ; : divisi in factiones, et saep.—
Transf.
For distribuere, to divide among several, to distribute, apportion: praedam,: argentum,: pecudes et agros,; cf. agros,: agrum viritim,; cf.: bona viritim,: munera, vestem, aurum, etc., et saep.: nummos in viros,: Thracia in Rhoemetalcen inque liberos Cotyis dividitur,; cf. . So of distributing troops in any place: equitatum in omnes partes,: exercitum omnem passim in civitates,; cf. : Romanos in custodiam civitatium,; cf. ; cf. also: conjuratos municipatim,: agros viritim civibus,; so with dat. (most freq.): agrum sordidissimo cuique,; cf. ; et saep.: tabellas toti Italiae,: praedam militibus,: loca praefectis,: duo praedia natis duobus,: oscula nulli, et saep.; cf. in double construction: divisit in singulos milites trecenos aeris, duplex centurionibus, triplex equiti,: inter participes praedam,; so, inter se,; : per populum fumantia (liba),; so, agros per veteranos,: dimidiam partem cum aliquo,; so ; : praemia mecum,.—Absol.: non divides (with dispertire),; so ; —
In mercant. lang. like distrahere and divendere, to sell piecemeal, in parcels, to retail, ; .—
In mal. part., Wagner; 7; cf. Büch.—
Trop.
In gen.: bona tripartito,: annum ex aequo,: horas (bucina),: tempora curarum remissionumque,: dignitatem ordinum,: et explanare ambigua,: idem genus universum in species certas partietur et dividet,; cf. of logical or rhet. division,; et saep.: verba, to divide at the end of the line, : nos alio mentes, alio divisimus aures,; cf.: animum nunc huc celerem, nunc dividit illuc,.—
In partic.
Sententiam, polit. t. t., to divide the question, i. e. to take the vote separately upon the several parts of a motion or proposition: divisa sententia est postulante nescio quo,; ; ; ; . The expression used in requiring this was DIVIDE, .—
(Acc. to A. 2. a.) To distribute, apportion: sic belli rationem esse divisam, ut, etc.,: haec temporibus,; Just. Praef. § 3: ea (negotia) divisa hoc modo dicebantur, etc.,.—
Pregn., to break up, dissolve, destroy = dissolvere: nostrum concentum,: ira fuit capitalis ut ultima divideret mors,: dividitur ferro regnum,; cf.: dividimus muros, et moenia pandimus urbis,.—
To accompany, i. e. to share upon an instrument a song sung by a voice: grata feminis Imbelli cithara carmina divides,.
To divide, separate, part from; to remove from (class.).
Lit.: flumen Rhenus agrum Helvetium a Germanis dividit ... flumen Rhodanus provinciam nostram ab Helvetiis dividit,; ; : Macedoniam a Thessalia,: Gallos ab Aquitanis,: tota cervice desecta, divisa a corpore capita,: populum distribuit in quinque classes, senioresque a junioribus divisit,: tam multa illa meo divisast milia lecto, Quantum, etc.,; cf.: dextras miseris complexibus,: tuis toto dividor orbe rogis,: dividor (sc.: ab uxore) haud aliter, quam si mea membra relinquam,; cf. : (Italiam) Longa procul longis via dividit invia terris,separates, keeps distant,; cf. : discedite a contactu ac dividite turbidos,—
Trop., to separate, distinguish: legem bonam a mala,: defensionem (opp. se comitem exitii promittebat),. —
Transf., for distinguere (II.), to distinguish, decorate, adorn (very rare): qualis gemma micat, fulvum quae dividit aurum,: scutulis dividere,.—Hence, dīvīsus, a, um, P. a., divided, separated: divisior,.—Adv.
dīvīse, distinctly, separately, ; fin.; .—
dīvīsim, separately, .

la:adj:dividus.html:
dīvĭdus, a, um, adj.
divido
,
separated: nosque ut sevorsum dividos leto offeres, Att. ap. (Trag. v. 118 Rib.: separatos, Non.).

la:adj:divinus.gloss: divine, of a deity, superhuman, supernatural
senses: divine, of a deity, superhuman, supernatural
la:adj:divinus.html:
dīvīnus, a, um, adj.
divus
,
of or belonging to a deity, divine (class. and very freq.).
Prop.: divinae Matris imago,: numen,; ; ; al.: stirps,; ; cf. semen,; and, origo,: Pergamum divina moenitum manu,; cf.: non sine ope divina bellum gerere,; and: quasi divino consilio,: stellae divinis animatae mentibus,: divina studia colere,: animos hominum esse divinos, i. e.,of divine origin,; cf.: hoc divinum animal (homo, shortly before: quasi mortalem deum), id.

Fin. 2, 13, 40: aliquis instinctus inflatusque,; cf.: causa divinior, et saep.: condimenta,enjoyed by the gods, divine,: odor (Veneris),; cf. decoris,: ars Palladis, et saep.: divinissima dona, i. e.,most worthy of a deity,: re divina facta, i. e., religious exercise, divine worship, sacrifice, etc., ; in this sense res divina is very freq.,; et saep.; ; ; ; ; ; ; et saep.; less freq. in the plur. divinae res, ; ; ; .—In plur. also in gen. for religious affairs, ; ; —Also verba, a form of prayer, : religiones (opp. fides humana),; cf. .—

Freq. connected with humanus as a stronger designation for all things, things of every kind, etc. (cf.: di hominesque under deus, I. B. fin.): dedunt se, divina humanaque omnia,; cf. ; ; : res,: jura,; : scelera,; cf. : spes, et saep. But in the explanation of philosophia by scientia divinarum humanarumque rerum, the term divinae res denotes nature, physics, as distinguished from humanae res, i. e. morals, ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; cf. ; .—So too in jurid. lang., divinae res signifies natural laws, in opp. to humanae res, positive laws, ; ; .—dīvīnum, i, n.,
The deity, τό θεῖον: divina si faverint,God willing,; ; ; —
The divine, that which comes from God, nihil est divino divinius, .—
That which is under the sanction of a god; hence: quicquam divini credere alicui; or simply: divini alicui credere, to believe one upon oath (ante-class.): numquam edepol tu mihi divini quicquam creduis, in, etc.,: quid ei divini aut humani aequum est credere?: nam mihi divini numquam quisquam creduat, ni, etc.,; .
Transf.
Divinely inspired, prophetic: aliquid praesagiens atque divinum,: animus appropinquante morte multo est divinior, etc.,; cf. fin.: cum ille potius divinus fuerit,: divinarum sagacem flammarum,: divini quicquam,; cf. ; also joined to humani,; .—Poet. of poets: vates,; cf.: divini pectoris carmina,.—With gen.: divina futuri Sententia,: avis imbrium imminentium,.— Subst.: dīvīnus, i, m., a soothsayer, prophet = vates, ; ; ; ; ; —In the fem.: dīvīna, ae, a prophetess, .—
Like caelestis (but far more freq. in prose), godlike, superhuman, admirable, excellent: ex maxime raro genere hominum et paene divino,: ingenio esse divino,: magni cujusdam civis et divini viri,; cf.: caelestes divinaeque legiones,: senatus in supplicatione deneganda,: homo in dicendo,: homo, Crispus ap. : orator, et saep.: incredibilis quaedam et divina virtus,: fides,: admurmuratio senatus,: memoria,: eloquentia M. Tullii,: facultas eloquendi,: ille nitor loquendi,: illa ironia,: haec in te, Sulpici, divina sunt, et saep.—In the comp.: ratione nihil est in homine divinius,; . Under the empire an epithet often bestowed on the emperors: domus,: princeps,; cf. ; : indulgentia, et saep.—Adv.: dīvīne.
(Acc. to I.) In a godlike manner, through godlike power: nunc tu divine fac huc assis Sosia,.—
(Acc. to II.)
By divine inspiration, prophetically: plura divine praesensa et praedicta reperiri,; ; and in the comp., Mos. —
In a godlike, superhuman, admirable manner, divinely: divine Plato escam malorum appellat voluptatem,; ; .—Sup. does not occur.

la:verb:divino.html:
dīvīno, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
divinus, II. A.
,
to foresee, divine; also, to foretell, predict, prophesy (class. cf. vaticino, praedico): non equidem hoc divinavi,: ut nihil boni divinet animus,; cf.: quod mens sua sponte divinat,; and: animo non divinante futura,: immortalitatem alicui,: permulta collecta sunt ab Antipatro, quae mirabiliter a Socrate divinata sunt,; cf.: divinatae opes,.—With acc. and inf.: neque ego ea, quae facta sunt, divinabam futura,; so ; ; ; et saep.—With rel. clause: divinare, quid in castris obvenisset,; so ; .—Absol.: Venus faciat eam, ut divinaret,; so ; ; ; et saep.; ; ; : si de exitu divinaret,: quaestum praestare divinando,.

la:adv:divinitus.gloss: from the gods, from heaven, by divine action
senses: from the gods, from heaven, by divine action
la:adv:divinitus.html:
dīvīnĭtus, adv.
id.
,
from heaven, by divine providence or influence (class.).
Prop.: divinitus latae suppetiae,; cf.: non partum per nos, sed divinitus ad nos delatum,: ; : divinitus accidere,: velut prodigio divinitus facto,: forte quadam divinitus super ripas Tiberis effusus,: casu quodam an divinitus,; cf.: seu forte seu divinitus,: quia sit divinitus illis Ingenium,.—
Transf.
By divine communication, by inspiration, prophetically: solus hic homo'st, qui sciat divinitus,; ; ; ; ; and opp. conjectura, Ruhnk.: inspirata,.—
Divinely, admirably, excellently (mostly Ciceronian): quae philosophi divinitus ferunt esse dicta,: dicta,; ; cf.: loquitur Pompeius,: scripta,: ille locus inductus a me,: meriti homines de me,: corpus humare,.

la:noun:divisio.html:
dīvīsĭo, ōnis, f.
id.
,
a division, separation.
Lit. (very rare).
In gen.: si divisio fieret,: animae ac spiritus,.—
In partic.
I. q. distributio, partition, distribution: agrorum,.—
Concr., an allotment, portion of food, etc., ; : POPVLO VIRITIM DIVISIONEM DEDIT, Inscr. Mommsen, 73; cf. ; .—
In mal. part., a violation, dishonoring, acc. to , and .—
Differences, subjects of dispute: diversa, quae divisiones multiplices ingerebant,.—
Trop., logical or rhetorical division (freq. in Cic. and Quint.), ; ; ; ; ; : De divisione, etc.

la:adj:dives.html:
dīves, ĭtis, and dīs, dīte (v. seq. β), adj.
perh. root div-, gleam; Gr. δῖος; Lat. divus, dies
,
rich (cf.: pecuniosus, beatus, locuples, opulens, opulentus).
dīves (class. and freq.; the nom. and acc. of the neutr. plur. do not occur; cf. Neue Formenl. 2, 51, v.
infra; abl. sing. usually divite, e. g. ; ; ; ; ; ; ; et saep.: diviti,; ): ubi dives blande appellat pauperem,; opp. pauper,; 49; ; ; et saep.: quem intelligimus divitem? etc.,: solos sapientes esse, si mendicissimi, divites,; so opp. mendici, et saep.: Crassus, cum cognomine dives tum copiis, ; cf.: Fufidius Dives agris, dives positis in fenore nummis,; ; so with abl.: pecore et multa tellure,: antiquo censu,: Lare,: amico Hercule,: auro,; ; ; cf. Liv. Praef. § 11: bubus,: dote, et saep.: dives pecoris nivei,; so with gen.: opum,; ; ; : armenti,: equum pictae vestis et auri,: artium, et saep.: dives ab omni armento,.—
Transf., of things.
Rich, sumptuous, costly, splendid, precious: animus hominis dives, non arca appellari solet,: Capua,: Anagnia,: Achaia,: ager,: ramus,: mensae,: lingua,: vena, et saep.: templum donis dives,: Africa triumphis,: Mantua avis, id. : terra amomo, et saep.: dives opis natura suae,.—
Abundant, plentiful (poet.): dives copia fiendi,; cf. stipendia,.

la:noun:divus.html:
dīvus, a, um, also dīus, a, um, (without the digamma) adj.
δῖος
,
of or belonging to a deity, divine.
Prop. (mostly archaic and poet.). As an adj. very rarely: res

divas edicit, Naev. ap. ; so, diva caro,: DIUM fulgur appellabant diurnum, quod putabant Jovis, ut nocturnum Summani, Paul. ex Müll.—Far more freq.,

Subst.: dīvus (dīus), i, m., and dīva (dia), ae, f., a god, a goddess, a deity.
Form dīvus: si divus, si diva, esset, etc., a precatory formula in ; cf. ; : is divus (sc. Apollo) exstinguet perduelles vestros, Carm. Marcii,; cf.: dive, quem proles Niobea, etc.,: mortalin' decuit violari vulnere divum?: utinam me divi adaxint ad suspendium,: divi,; ; ; : divos,; ; ; ; ; et saep.: divumque hominumque pater, rex, Enn. ap. Müll.; ; ; et saep.: divom atque hominum clamat fidem,; cf.: pro divum fidem,; more rarely, divorum,: (munera) digna diva venustissima Venere,: Turni sic est affata sororem Diva deam,i. e. Juno,; cf. ; 482: Diva Bona for Bona Dea,: divos scelerare parentes, the family gods = θεοί πατρῶοι, .—
Form dīus: Dii Indigetes Diique Manes, a precatory formula in : Dia Dearum, Enn. ap. Müll. (Ann. v. 22, ed. Vahl.); cf.: DEA DIA,i. e. Ceres, and 1499: Venus pulcherrima dium, Enn. ap. Prob. ap. .—
Transf.
Godlike, divine, an epithet applied to any thing deified or of extraordinary excellence or distinction: urbi Romae divae,; cf. sarcastically: est ergo flamen, ut Jovi, etc., sic divo Julio M. Antonius,: Romule die, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 115, ed. Vahl.): Ilia dia nepos, id. ap. Müll. (Ann. v. 56, ed. Vahl.): dia Camilla,: dias in luminis oras,; so, Voluptas,: otia,: profundum (cf. ἅλς δῖα), : sententia Catonis,: poëmata, et saep.—After the Aug. period divus became a frequent epithet for the deceased Roman emperors in the historians, and on coins and inscriptions, ; .—
dīvum, i, n., the sky, Müll.—Esp. freq., sub divo, like sub Jove, under the open sky, in the open air, Zumpt N. cr.; l. l.; ; ; ; et saep.: sub divum rapiam,.

la:verb:divello.gloss: to rend; tear apart, asunder, away or in pieces; remove
senses: to rend; tear apart, asunder, away or in pieces; remove
la:verb:divello.html:
dī-vello, velli (;
but divulsi,), vulsum, 3, v. a.
To rend asunder, to tear in pieces, to separate violently, to tear (class.; cf.: findo, scindo, dirimo, segrego, secerno).
Lit.: res a natura copulatas audebit divellere,: corpus, et undis spargere,; so, corpus,: agnam,; cf.: suos artus lacero morsu,: membra,; et saep.: magnos montes manibus,i. e. to cleave,; cf.: mediam partem quercus (with discidere),: nodos manibus,to untie,: paenulam sentibus,: nubem,; cf.: moenia mundi,.—
Trop., to tear violently apart, remove, destroy, sunder: commoda civium,: rem dissolutam divulsamque conglutinare,; cf. : affinitas divelli nullo modo poterat,to be dissolved, destroyed,; cf. amicitiam,; and: amorem querimoniis,: somnos (cura),: distineor et divellor dolore,am distracted,.—
(Like distraho, II.) To tear away, separate, remove from something (class.).
Lit.: membra divellere ac distrahere,: aliquem ab aliquo,; : liberos a parentum complexu,; for which: aliquem dulci amplexu,; cf.: Damalin adultero,: nec me umquam Gyas (sc. a te),.—
Trop.: sapientiam, temperantiam, a voluptate divellere ac distrahere,. —So of persons, to draw away from one in feeling, to estrange: qui a me mei servatorem capitis divellat ac distrahat,.

la:verb:diverto.html:
dī-verto (vorto), ti, sum, 3, v. n.,
to turn or go different ways, to part, separate, turn aside (in the verb. finit. rare; not in the class. per.).
Lit.
To turn out of the way; hence, of travellers, to stop, lodge, sojourn: qui divertebat in proximo,: in cenaculum,: ad hominem peccatorem,to visit,—
Of a married woman, to leave her husband: (uxor) sive diverterit, sive nupta est adhuc,; cf. so of divorce: si uxor a legato diverterit,: nullis matrimoniis divertentibus,. V. also divortium.—
Trop., to deviate from each other, to differ: divortunt mores virgini longe ac lupae,.—Hence, dīversus (-vorsus), a, um, P. a., turned different ways.
Set over against each other, opposite, contrary (freq. and class.; cf.: adversus, contrarius).
Lit.: in diversum iter equi concitati,: fenestrae,opposite each other,; cf. ripa, Drak.: iter a proposito diversum,; cf.: diverso ab ea regione itinere,: diversis ab flumine regionibus,: diversam aciem constituit,: duo cinguli maxime inter se diversi, i. e. the two polar circles, (13): diversum ad mare dejectus,; cf.: procurrentibus in diversa terris,: in diversum flectere,: binas per diversum coassationes substernere,cross-wise,.—
Trop.

root vidh-, to part, split; Sanscr. vidhyati, to penetrate, whence vidhava; Lat. vidua
.
To force asunder, part, separate, divide (very freq. and class.; cf.: distribuo, dispertio; findo, scindo, dirimo, divello, separo, sejungo, segrego, secerno).
Lit.: Europam Libyamque rapax ubi dividit unda, Enn. ap. ; and : discludere mundum membraque dividere,; cf.: si omne animal secari ac dividi potest, nullum est eorum individuum,: crassum aërem, (with perrumpere); cf. nubila,: muros,to break through,: marmor cuneis,to split,; cf.: hunc medium securi,: mediam frontem ferro,; also simply, insulam, for to divide into two parts, .—Poet.: vagam caelo volucrem,i. e. to cleave, to shoot,: sol ... in partes non aequas dividit orbem,; so Galliam in partes tres,: vicum in duas partes flumine,: civitatem Helvetiam in quatuor pagos,: populum unum in duas partes,; cf. ; : divisi in factiones, et saep.—
Transf.
For distribuere, to divide among several, to distribute, apportion: praedam,: argentum,: pecudes et agros,; cf. agros,: agrum viritim,; cf.: bona viritim,: munera, vestem, aurum, etc., et saep.: nummos in viros,: Thracia in Rhoemetalcen inque liberos Cotyis dividitur,; cf. . So of distributing troops in any place: equitatum in omnes partes,: exercitum omnem passim in civitates,; cf. : Romanos in custodiam civitatium,; cf. ; cf. also: conjuratos municipatim,: agros viritim civibus,; so with dat. (most freq.): agrum sordidissimo cuique,; cf. ; et saep.: tabellas toti Italiae,: praedam militibus,: loca praefectis,: duo praedia natis duobus,: oscula nulli, et saep.; cf. in double construction: divisit in singulos milites trecenos aeris, duplex centurionibus, triplex equiti,: inter participes praedam,; so, inter se,; : per populum fumantia (liba),; so, agros per veteranos,: dimidiam partem cum aliquo,; so ; : praemia mecum,.—Absol.: non divides (with dispertire),; so ; —
In mercant. lang. like distrahere and divendere, to sell piecemeal, in parcels, to retail, ; .—
In mal. part., Wagner; 7; cf. Büch.—
Trop.
In gen.: bona tripartito,: annum ex aequo,: horas (bucina),: tempora curarum remissionumque,: dignitatem ordinum,: et explanare ambigua,: idem genus universum in species certas partietur et dividet,; cf. of logical or rhet. division,; et saep.: verba, to divide at the end of the line, : nos alio mentes, alio divisimus aures,; cf.: animum nunc huc celerem, nunc dividit illuc,.—
In partic.
Sententiam, polit. t. t., to divide the question, i. e. to take the vote separately upon the several parts of a motion or proposition: divisa sententia est postulante nescio quo,; ; ; ; . The expression used in requiring this was DIVIDE, .—
(Acc. to A. 2. a.) To distribute, apportion: sic belli rationem esse divisam, ut, etc.,: haec temporibus,; Just. Praef. § 3: ea (negotia) divisa hoc modo dicebantur, etc.,.—
Pregn., to break up, dissolve, destroy = dissolvere: nostrum concentum,: ira fuit capitalis ut ultima divideret mors,: dividitur ferro regnum,; cf.: dividimus muros, et moenia pandimus urbis,.—
To accompany, i. e. to share upon an instrument a song sung by a voice: grata feminis Imbelli cithara carmina divides,.
To divide, separate, part from; to remove from (class.).
Lit.: flumen Rhenus agrum Helvetium a Germanis dividit ... flumen Rhodanus provinciam nostram ab Helvetiis dividit,; ; : Macedoniam a Thessalia,: Gallos ab Aquitanis,: tota cervice desecta, divisa a corpore capita,: populum distribuit in quinque classes, senioresque a junioribus divisit,: tam multa illa meo divisast milia lecto, Quantum, etc.,; cf.: dextras miseris complexibus,: tuis toto dividor orbe rogis,: dividor (sc.: ab uxore) haud aliter, quam si mea membra relinquam,; cf. : (Italiam) Longa procul longis via dividit invia terris,separates, keeps distant,; cf. : discedite a contactu ac dividite turbidos,—
Trop., to separate, distinguish: legem bonam a mala,: defensionem (opp. se comitem exitii promittebat),. —
Transf., for distinguere (II.), to distinguish, decorate, adorn (very rare): qualis gemma micat, fulvum quae dividit aurum,: scutulis dividere,.—Hence, dīvīsus, a, um, P. a., divided, separated: divisior,.—Adv.
dīvīse, distinctly, separately, ; fin.; .—
dīvīsim, separately, .

Lit.: flumen Rhenus agrum Helvetium a Germanis dividit ... flumen Rhodanus provinciam nostram ab Helvetiis dividit,; ; : Macedoniam a Thessalia,: Gallos ab Aquitanis,: tota cervice desecta, divisa a corpore capita,: populum distribuit in quinque classes, senioresque a junioribus divisit,: tam multa illa meo divisast milia lecto, Quantum, etc.,; cf.: dextras miseris complexibus,: tuis toto dividor orbe rogis,: dividor (sc.: ab uxore) haud aliter, quam si mea membra relinquam,; cf. : (Italiam) Longa procul longis via dividit invia terris,separates, keeps distant,; cf. : discedite a contactu ac dividite turbidos,—
Trop., to separate, distinguish: legem bonam a mala,: defensionem (opp. se comitem exitii promittebat),. —
Transf., for distinguere (II.), to distinguish, decorate, adorn (very rare): qualis gemma micat, fulvum quae dividit aurum,: scutulis dividere,.—Hence, dīvīsus, a, um, P. a., divided, separated: divisior,.—Adv.
dīvīse, distinctly, separately, ; fin.; .—
dīvīsim, separately, .

la:verb:divello#3.html:
dī-vello, velli (;
but divulsi,), vulsum, 3, v. a.
To rend asunder, to tear in pieces, to separate violently, to tear (class.; cf.: findo, scindo, dirimo, segrego, secerno).
Lit.: res a natura copulatas audebit divellere,: corpus, et undis spargere,; so, corpus,: agnam,; cf.: suos artus lacero morsu,: membra,; et saep.: magnos montes manibus,i. e. to cleave,; cf.: mediam partem quercus (with discidere),: nodos manibus,to untie,: paenulam sentibus,: nubem,; cf.: moenia mundi,.—
Trop., to tear violently apart, remove, destroy, sunder: commoda civium,: rem dissolutam divulsamque conglutinare,; cf. : affinitas divelli nullo modo poterat,to be dissolved, destroyed,; cf. amicitiam,; and: amorem querimoniis,: somnos (cura),: distineor et divellor dolore,am distracted,.—
(Like distraho, II.) To tear away, separate, remove from something (class.).
Lit.: membra divellere ac distrahere,: aliquem ab aliquo,; : liberos a parentum complexu,; for which: aliquem dulci amplexu,; cf.: Damalin adultero,: nec me umquam Gyas (sc. a te),.—
Trop.: sapientiam, temperantiam, a voluptate divellere ac distrahere,. —So of persons, to draw away from one in feeling, to estrange: qui a me mei servatorem capitis divellat ac distrahat,.
